title: Models that say more, and instances that connect
summary: With 1.6.0, a model tells you more about how to print it and what you may do with it. Print profiles show on the model page with their print time, filament and plates, laid out the way each person picks, and every model keeps the licence it was published under, filtered by what it allows and written beside its files. And Thingport instances connect with each other: pair yours with a friend's, a makerspace's or the one at work, and their people's models, collections and profiles show up on your Explore, to download, open in a slicer or copy, with chats across both. One at home connects to one on the internet with no port forwarding. PIXUP, Fab365 and 3DExport bring the sites Thingport imports from to twenty-one, collections can be shared with just the people you pick, profiles get covers and avatars, and the app speaks Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian.

items.title: Print profiles on the model page, shown the way you like
items.description: A model imported with its print profiles, from MakerWorld, Snapmaker Space, Creality Cloud, NexPrint or MakerOnline, now shows them as profiles above Open rather than as a row of 3MF files. Each has its name, whether the designer or the community made it, with the designer's first, its print time, filament by colour and weight, its plates with their pictures, and the printer, nozzle, layer height, infill and walls, read from the site and from the profile's own 3MF. The 3D preview shows the picked profile's plates. Everyone chooses how they look under Configuration → Appearance → Print profiles: a Picker like the file picker, with the picked profile's numbers below it, which is the default; a List of every profile at once; Tiles of their pictures; or Off, for plain files as before. Models imported earlier read their profiles the first time their owner opens them, and new imports a few seconds after they arrive. Downloads, likes and ratings are left out on purpose: what's shown is what helps you print.

images.caption: Picker, the default: the picked profile's time, filament, plates and settings
Tiles: each profile by its picture

items.title: Connect your Thingport instance with others
items.description: Thingport instances can now connect, so the people on them find, open and copy each other's models and write to each other as if they were on one instance: your home instance with a friend's, your makerspace's or the one at work. Partners' people, public collections and newest models show up on Explore beside yours, each marked with its instance, and Everywhere, This instance or one partner narrows it down. A partner's model opens with its pictures, description, files and collections: download it file by file or as a ZIP, open it in your slicer, or Copy to my library to keep your own, with its tags, print profiles, licence and the site it came from. A partner's people have profiles like anyone here, and can be written to, added to private rooms and shared a collection with. Everyone gets a handle, name@their.instance, and can ask to reach someone on an instance that isn't a partner yet, which goes to the admins. It's off until an admin turns it on under Administration → Social, with social features on, and admins on both sides approve every partner after comparing a key. Nothing private crosses: libraries, private collections, settings and emails stay where they are. It runs over ActivityPub, between Thingport instances only, and works over plain HTTP too.

images.caption: Explore, everywhere: people and models from this instance and a partner, each marked with its instance
A partner's model, to download, open in a slicer or copy

items.title: An instance at home connects too, with no port forwarding
items.description: Most home instances can't be reached from the internet: the router in front of them turns away whatever nobody inside asked for, which would leave them without partners. So an instance at home reaches out to its partner on the internet and keeps a link open to it, and whatever the partner would send it or fetch from it comes back down that link. No port forwarding, domain or certificate: a Raspberry Pi, a NAS or an old laptop is enough, and only the instance on the internet needs an address others can reach. Explore, pictures, downloads, copies and chats work both ways through it. Connecting from an instance that's on your network only, or that nothing can reach, turns Keep a link open on by itself and says why, and Partners shows whether each link is open. While the home instance is off, what's said to its people waits on the partner's side for up to about three days, and arrives once its link opens again. Its own address is never tried from the other side. Two instances on one network connect directly, as any two that reach each other do. Two that are both at home can't reach each other: put them on one VPN, such as Tailscale or WireGuard, and they connect as two instances on one network.

images.caption: Connecting from home: the partner's key to compare, and Keep a link open
Partners under Administration → Social, a home instance with its link open

items.title: Every model keeps its licence
items.description: What you may do with a model, whether you may share its files, remix it or sell prints of it, now comes with it. Every site Thingport imports from says what licence a model has, and the import keeps it: Creative Commons licences, CC0, open-source ones such as GPL and MIT, and each site's own. A strip at the foot of the description box shows its marks and what it comes to, such as "Credit · Non-commercial · Share alike", and opens what it lets you do, the terms the site or the creator added, a link to the licence and Copy credit line. Edit has a Licence field, for a model you uploaded or one you've made your own, and a licence you pick is never read over. The filter on every list of models gains Licence allows: Can be shared, Commercial use, Remixing and Only with a licence, which combine. Each model with a licence gets a LICENSE.txt beside its files, with the credit line, and every ZIP download carries one; admins can turn the files off under Administration → Storage → Licence files. Copies, connected instances and the MCP tools carry the licence too. Models imported earlier read theirs the first time you open them. A licence only informs: nothing is blocked or warned about because of one.

images.caption: A model's licence: what it allows, its terms and a credit line to copy
Licence allows, in every list's filter

items.title: Import from PIXUP, Fab365 and 3DExport: twenty-one sites
items.description: Three more sites to import from, each signed in to per person, through Thingport Grab or by pasting the sign-in, with no FlareSolverr needed. PIXUP, Phrozen's marketplace: free models and the ones you bought, anyone's wishlists and your collections, synced too. PIXUP hands over a free model's files only once it's in your account, so Thingport checks it out at $0 through your cart, as long as everything in the cart is free. Fab365: free models and the ones you own, bought or redeemed with a ticket, and your favourites, synced too; Thingport never spends money or tickets, and keeps renewing your sign-in itself. 3DExport, one of the oldest marketplaces: free and bought models, with their STL, 3MF, STEP and LightBurn files and a CG model's scenes and textures left behind, and your Default Collection and your own or anyone's public collections, synced too. Each brings its categories, trending models and licence, and all three are on for everyone after the update.

images.caption: Administration → Providers, newest first: 3DExport, Fab365 and PIXUP

items.title: Share a collection with just the people you pick
items.description: A collection's form now offers Private, Shared or Public. Shared shows it only to the people you pick, by any part of their name or their whole email, or by their handle on a connected instance: they see it as they would a public one, with its models to open, download, open in a slicer and copy, and nobody else on your instance sees it. Shared with someone on a connected instance, it's sent to theirs, whose admins could see it too. They're told, and find it under Shared with you, at the top of Explore. Share… on a collection's ⋮ menu opens the form on who sees it. You see who it's shared with on its cover and beside its name; they don't see who else is on the list. Add or take people off at any time, and the list stays when you make the collection private or public, for the next time you share it. Up to 100 people a collection, with social features on.

images.caption: Private, Shared or Public, and who it's shared with
Shared with you, at the top of Explore

items.title: Profiles with a cover, an avatar, a bio and links
items.description: Edit profile, on My models, gives everyone a cover, a bio of up to 1,000 characters in Markdown and up to five links. A cover is one of five drawn designs, retro, pixel art, mosaic, ASCII or blueprint, a linked account's cover, or a picture of your own, cropped to fit. Click your avatar to design one from hair, glasses, expressions and colours, or to upload a picture. Left alone, it's your Gravatar, fetched by your instance so nobody else learns your email from it, or one drawn for you. With social features on, the lock beside Edit profile puts My models on Explore: your uploads and your linked authors' models, for others to open, download and copy. Someone's profile on Explore opens on their models, with their collections beside them.

images.caption: A profile: cover, avatar, bio and links
Design an avatar, or use a picture or your Gravatar

items.title: Русский, Українська and Беларуская
items.description: Thingport, its nine built-in tools and the weather widget now speak Russian, Ukrainian and Belarusian, each with its own plural forms, thanks to krolbot (#280). Configuration → Appearance → Language is a list to search, with each language's flag, its own name and how much of the app it covers, and import notifications are titled in your language too.

images.caption: Seven languages, by flag, name and how much is translated

items.title: A copy is the whole model
items.description: Adding someone else's model to a collection of yours, or copying one from a connected instance, now brings all of it: its category, as your own category of the same name when you have one, or for AI categorization to sort if that's on, the site it came from, its print profiles and its pictures, with a partner's description images kept on your instance. If you already have the model from that site, yours opens instead of a second copy.

items.title: Pick how Thingport Grab looks on a page
items.description: Grab's popup has an Appearance tab once it's connected: six looks for its button on a model page, Bubble, Pill, Mini, Brand, Glass and Edge tab, in any of the four corners, changing as you pick. The button now shows on every model page: a tick and a green ring when the model is in your library, opening it there, and a + when part of it is, such as some of its print profiles. Grab then adds just the missing ones, so a site's daily download limit isn't spent on the profiles you have. The sites you've turned on, and your instance's address, are links in the popup.

images.caption: Grab's Appearance tab: a look and a corner for its button

items.title: Open in a slicer through Thingport Bridge, when the slicer can't reach your instance
items.description: Some slicers can't download from an instance themselves, over a certificate they don't trust, for one. Right-click a slicer under Configuration → Slicer and turn on Through Thingport Bridge, and opening a model in that slicer goes through Bridge on your computer, marked with a cable on the slicer's tile. It works for OrcaSlicer, Creality Print, Elegoo Slicer, Snapmaker Orca and eufyMake Studio. The new Bridge fetches only model files, opens them directly rather than through cmd on Windows, keeps session tokens out of its log, and finds those slicers where they're installed, Creality Print 7 included. Thanks to pike338 (#287).

items.title: Administration → Social, for what people share
items.description: Social features and chats moved from the Users page to a page of their own, after Users, which also switches connected instances on and holds their requests, partners and blocked instances.

items.title: Administration → Providers, as cards
items.description: Each site is a card: its logo and name, what it imports, such as collections, likes, print profiles or paid models, who signs in, and what it needs, such as Thingport Grab or FlareSolverr. Sort by newest, oldest or name, filter by any of those, and turn several on or off at once with Select providers, shift-clicking for a range.

items.title: Delete all of someone's models, and no more Triggers page
items.description: A person's ⋮ menu under Administration → Users has Delete all models, confirmed by typing their email, which keeps their account, collections and categories. Any admin can do it to a member, only the owner to another admin, and nobody to the owner. Administration → Triggers is gone: authors are still linked as more of their models are imported, or one model at a time with Fetch missing details.

items.title: Earlier releases, from What's new
items.description: The history button at the top of What's new opens any earlier release's notes in place, with Back to latest to return, and an instance still on an older release is shown that release's own notes.

items.title: Every page opens at the top, and going back to a list of models returns to the same models at the same place, without loading them again
thingport.net has a new home page, built around a demo video of Thingport
Loading more models at the foot of a list no longer stalls
Grab's note on a part-finished print profile import ends with the last error, so you can see why the rest failed, thanks to truri83 (#265)
A tool's models and collections can no longer be changed through an address written another way, with a trailing slash or an encoded id
